about: What a scheduled task and a server folder run, as text: the task shims, the server launchers, the launchd plists, the systemd units and the schtasks command lines (Windows writes no Task Scheduler XML: the task is made with schtasks /Create and holds only the shim path). The text comes from SPAWNLOFT_ENTRY, the core's own path, so Rust can reproduce it and RUNTIME_FORMAT stays 2. test/contracts-files.test.mjs generates every text from the Node functions with the inputs below; "asserted" says how: live (the Node writer ran), source (the template was checked in the source and its formula run, because the writer only runs on another platform).

placeholders.<entry>: the spawnloft-core path: a 2.0 install, SPAWNLOFT_ENTRY set
placeholders.<node>: the running executable: a checkout or 1.x build, SPAWNLOFT_ENTRY unset
placeholders.<home>: $HOME of the process that wrote the shim
placeholders.<ns>: the first 16 hex digits of sha256(<data>), so two data folders on one machine do not share task names

task.enabledExceptHourly: the plist for hourly is written with enabled false, to show Disabled

posix.about: <data>/tasks/<id>.sh, mode 0700, run by launchd and systemd as /bin/sh <file> (schedule-mac.mjs writeShim; Linux uses the same). Exports SPAWNLOFT_DATA_ROOT, then the runner's own environment (ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 when not an entry binary: written for a 1.x desktop build, harmless under node), then HOME, APPDATA, XDG_CONFIG_HOME and XDG_DATA_HOME, each only if set in the writer's environment, in that order. Every value and argument is single-quoted, a quote inside written as '\''. LF.

entry.text:
#!/bin/sh
export SPAWNLOFT_DATA_ROOT='<data>'
export HOME='<home>'
export XDG_CONFIG_HOME='<config>'
exec '<entry>' task run 'survival-backup'

checkout.text:
#!/bin/sh
export SPAWNLOFT_DATA_ROOT='<data>'
export ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE='1'
export HOME='<home>'
export XDG_CONFIG_HOME='<config>'
exec '<node>' '<mcctl>' task run 'survival-backup'

windows.about: <data>\tasks\<id>.cmd (schedule.mjs writeShim): @echo off, entry.mjs windowsRun lines, exit /b %errorlevel%, joined and ended with CRLF. windowsRun: set KEY=VALUE for each runner variable, then the runner quoted (a checkout whose executable is node or node.exe writes bare node, a PATH lookup), each argument quoted, then the command; every % in a path or value doubled.

launchers.asserted: live (writeLaunchers, with process.platform set to each platform for the call)
launchers.about: start, console and stop in the server folder (create.mjs writeLaunchers): .sh on Linux, .bat on Windows and on macOS too (any platform but Linux). The .sh files are mode 0755 and single-quoted like the shims. The .bat files are a template literal in create.mjs: their lines end the way src/create.mjs is checked out (LF in an LF checkout, CRLF in a CRLF one), except windowsRun's set lines, which always end CRLF. The texts below are from an LF checkout; the test converts them when the source has CRLF.

console.bat.text:
@echo off
title survival console - SpawnLoft
"<entry>" console survival
pause

stop.bat.text:
@echo off
title survival - SpawnLoft
"<entry>" stop survival
pause

console.bat.text:
@echo off
title survival console - SpawnLoft
node "<mcctl>" console survival
pause

stop.bat.text:
@echo off
title survival - SpawnLoft
node "<mcctl>" stop survival
pause

launchd.about: ~/Library/LaunchAgents/<label>.plist, mode 0600 (schedule-mac.mjs plist): one line of plist XML after the two header lines, keys in this order, & < > " ' escaped in strings, ending with a newline. Weekday is 0 for Sunday. Loaded with launchctl bootstrap gui/<uid>; enabled or disabled with launchctl enable/disable gui/<uid>/<label>.

systemd.asserted: live (serviceUnit and timerUnit are pure); the systemctl calls are live on Linux with a stand-in systemctl
systemd.about: <config>/systemd/user/<label>.service and .timer, mode 0600 (schedule-linux.mjs). In units % is doubled everywhere; ExecStart's argument is double-quoted with \ and " escaped and $ doubled. onlogon has no timer: the service is WantedBy=default.target and enabled without --now.

minutes.service:
[Unit]
Description=SpawnLoft task survival-backup

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/bin/sh "<data>/tasks/survival-backup.sh"
WorkingDirectory=<data>
KillMode=process
StandardOutput=append:<data>/tasks/survival-backup.stdout.log
StandardError=append:<data>/tasks/survival-backup.stderr.log
minutes.timer:
[Unit]
Description=SpawnLoft schedule survival-backup

[Timer]
OnActiveSec=1800s
OnUnitActiveSec=1800s
AccuracySec=1s

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target

calls.about: systemctl --user, in this order, for a create of an enabled task and of a disabled one (update runs the same list as create). <label> is spawnloft-<ns>-<id>. The answers of is-active, is-enabled and disable are read but their exit codes are not checked.

schtasks.asserted: source (triggerArgs is evaluated from src/schedule.mjs; schtasks only runs on Windows)
schtasks.about: The Windows task is made and changed by running schtasks with these arguments (schedule.mjs). The task path is \mcctl\<id>; /TR holds the shim path in its own double quotes so a path with spaces survives; /F overwrites by name, which keeps the run history.
